title.en: Lesia Ukrainka · Writing across languages and imperial borders
title.zh: 莱霞·乌克兰卡 · 跨越语言与帝国边界的写作

location.label: Zviahel; birthplace, not the setting of every work

summary.en:
Lesia Ukrainka was the pen name of Larysa Kosach, born in Volhynia in 1871 into a family involved in Ukrainian writing and cultural debate. Her mother, the writer Olena Pchilka, helped shape an education combining private teaching, extensive reading and languages. Illness restricted her formal schooling and repeatedly took her away for treatment. It did not confine her intellectual world to one country or one literary tradition.

Her poems appeared in the Lviv journal Zoria in 1884. Translation, correspondence and literary groups connected her to other writers; work with Heine and other European authors expanded the possibilities of writing in Ukrainian. Her first original poetry collection appeared in Lviv in 1893, across the imperial border from the Russian-ruled lands where her family lived. The Kyiv edition of 1904 belongs to a later publishing setting, rather than proving that censorship had never mattered.

During her later career she developed poetic dramas that explored coercion, responsibility, belief and artistic freedom. Ancient and biblical settings let these works ask questions extending beyond contemporary political events. The Forest Song, written in 1911, drew on a remembered Volhynian cultural landscape while examining desire and everyday obligations. Her career therefore connects language politics to experiments in literary form, rather than making every character a simple national allegory. She died in Surami, Georgia, in 1913; later publication and interpretation continued after her life ended.
summary.zh:
莱霞·乌克兰卡是拉里萨·科萨奇的笔名。她1871年出生于沃里尼亚，家庭积极参与乌克兰文学与文化讨论。母亲、作家奥列娜·普奇尔卡帮助她接受结合私人教学、广泛阅读和语言学习的教育。疾病限制了她的正规求学，也使她多次外出治疗，却没有把她的思想世界局限于一个国家或一种文学传统。

1884年，她的诗作刊于利沃夫《曙光》杂志。翻译、通信和文学团体把她与其他作家相连；译介海涅等欧洲作者，也扩展了乌克兰语写作的可能。1893年，首部原创诗集在利沃夫出版，与家人居住的俄罗斯帝国统治地区隔着帝国边界。1904年的基辅版本属于另一出版情境，并不能证明审查从未产生影响。

后期创作中，她发展诗体戏剧，探讨强制、责任、信仰与艺术自由。古代及圣经背景使作品提出超越当时政治事件的问题。1911年写成的《森林之歌》借助记忆中的沃里尼亚文化景观，考察愿望与日常义务。因此，她的生涯把语言政治与文学形式实验联系起来，而非使每个人物都成为简单的民族寓言。1913年她在格鲁吉亚苏拉米去世，出版与阐释在其身后继续。

dateNote.en: Lifespan 1871–1913. Exact birth/death days differ in the inspected references, so only years are used. Lviv milestones mark publication, not proven personal presence; 1911 composition is discussed without inventing a writing-site pin.
dateNote.zh: 生卒1871—1913年。所查资料的具体生卒日存在差异，故仅用年份。利沃夫节点表示出版地点，不证明本人在场；1911年创作在正文说明，不虚构写作地点。

title.en: Ukrainian books · Censorship, translation and cross-border print
title.zh: 乌克兰语书籍 · 审查、翻译与跨境印刷

location.label: Lviv; representative publishing centre outside the Russian Empire

summary.en:
Ukrainian-language publishing in the late nineteenth century depended on the different institutions and restrictions on either side of an imperial border. The Ems decree of 1876 restricted printing and imports into the Russian Empire, along with theatrical performance, public readings and Ukrainian lyrics in printed music. Its rules included exceptions and censorship conditions: historical documents and literary works were not treated identically. Describing every Ukrainian book as absolutely prohibited conceals those distinctions.

Lviv, then within Austria-Hungary, offered a publishing setting for authors connected with Russian-ruled Ukraine. Lesia Ukrainka’s early poems appeared there in 1884, and her first poetry collection followed in 1893. Literary journals, translators, editors and correspondence helped sustain a reading world that cannot be represented by a single state capital. Her 1904 Kyiv edition supplies a further publication point, rather than a date when all restrictions disappeared.

This sequence invites comparison between the reach intended by a decree and the actual work of making books. It does not quantify circulation, establish that everyone could read or buy them, or turn the border into a reconstructed smuggling route.
summary.zh:
十九世纪后期的乌克兰语出版，依赖帝国边界两侧不同的制度与限制。1876年《埃姆斯敕令》限制俄罗斯帝国内的印刷与书籍输入，也限制乌克兰语戏剧、公读及印刷乐谱中的歌词。规则包含例外和审查条件，历史文献与文学作品并非一概同等处理。若称所有乌克兰语书籍都绝对禁止，就会掩盖这些区别。

当时属于奥匈帝国的利沃夫，为与俄治乌克兰相连的作家提供出版环境。莱霞·乌克兰卡1884年的早期诗作与1893年的首部诗集均在当地问世。文学期刊、译者、编辑与通信维持着无法用一个首都概括的阅读世界。1904年的基辅版本提供了另一个出版节点，并非一切限制消失的日期。

这一序列使读者能够比较法令意图控制的范围与实际制书工作。它不量化发行量，不说明人人都能识字或购书，也不把边界画成重建的走私路线。

dateNote.en: 1876–1904 is a selected window from the Ems decree to Ukrainka’s Kyiv second edition; it is not the beginning or end of Ukrainian print culture or a legal repeal interval.
dateNote.zh: 1876—1904年是从《埃姆斯敕令》到乌克兰卡基辅再版的选定时段，不是乌克兰语印刷文化的起止，也不是法令撤销时段。

title.en: Jan Amos Comenius · Education through exile and religious hope
title.zh: 扬·阿摩司·夸美纽斯 · 流亡与宗教希望中的教育

location.label: Uherský Brod region; representative birth region, exact birthplace disputed

summary.en:
Jan Amos Comenius, or Jan Ámos Komenský, was born in Moravia in 1592 and educated within the Unity of the Brethren and Protestant schools. A minister and teacher at Fulnek from 1618, he encountered the defeat of the Bohemian Protestant estates and the insecurity that followed. Hiding, family loss and exile formed the setting of his early literary and educational work, rather than a separate interruption to an otherwise settled scholarly career.

In 1628 he went to Leszno in Poland, where the Brethren’s institutions supported teaching and textbook production. He wanted language instruction to connect words with familiar things, and educational reform to form part of a wider improvement of human affairs. His pansophic ambitions were explicitly Christian. They should not be rewritten as a modern secular curriculum already adopted everywhere.

Correspondence and patrons connected him with England, Swedish projects and Transylvania. In 1650 he went to Sárospatak to attempt school reform; writing there contributed to the picture-based teaching associated with Orbis Pictus. The destruction of Leszno in 1656 brought another loss of books and manuscripts. Amsterdam offered refuge and patronage for his remaining years.

Orbis Pictus appeared in Nuremberg in 1658, combining language and illustrations; the publication city is not evidence that he lived there then. He died in Amsterdam in 1670. His story connects classrooms, confessional communities, printers and patrons across political frontiers while leaving the success and reach of his proposals open to evidence.
summary.zh:
扬·阿摩司·夸美纽斯1592年生于摩拉维亚，在兄弟会及新教学校接受教育。1618年起在富尔内克任牧师和教师，随后经历波希米亚新教等级势力的失败与动荡。躲藏、亲人去世及流亡构成早期文学与教育著述的环境，而非一段安定学术生涯之外的偶然插曲。

1628年他迁往波兰莱什诺，兄弟会的机构支持教学和教材制作。他希望语言学习把词语与熟悉的事物相连，并把教育改革纳入改善人类事务的更大计划。其泛智思想具有明确的基督教基础，不能改写成已在各地实施的现代世俗课程。

通信与资助者使他与英格兰、瑞典相关项目及特兰西瓦尼亚相连。1650年他赴沙罗什保陶克尝试学校改革，当地写作也参与形成后来《世界图解》的图像教学。1656年莱什诺被毁，他再次失去书籍和手稿；阿姆斯特丹为余生提供庇护与支持。

1658年《世界图解》在纽伦堡出版，将语言与图像结合；出版城市不证明作者当时居于当地。1670年他在阿姆斯特丹去世。这一生平把政治边界两侧的课堂、宗教社群、印刷者与资助人相连，同时将改革建议的成效与传播范围留待证据检验。

dateNote.en: Lifespan 1592–1670. The museum identifies an uncertain birthplace within the Uherský Brod region. Milestones mark institutional settings; Nuremberg in 1658 means book publication, not the author’s presence.
dateNote.zh: 生卒1592—1670年。博物馆说明具体出生地在乌赫尔斯基布罗德地区内仍有争议。节点表示机构环境；1658年纽伦堡表示书籍出版，不表示作者在场。

title.en: Orbis Pictus · Words, pictures and the familiar world
title.zh: 《世界图解》 · 词语、图像与熟悉的世界

summary.en:
Orbis Sensualium Pictus joined illustrations with vocabulary to make the visible world part of language learning. The original Latin–German edition appeared in Nuremberg in 1658; a Latin–English edition followed in London in 1659. These publication dates mark selected editions, rather than the birth of illustrated teaching or the end of the book’s use.

Comenius’s design connected learning with familiar things. The University of Minnesota’s exhibition describes subjects including geography, weather, plants, animals and machinery alongside spiritual matters. An illustrated page offered a way to discuss words through objects and activities, rather than treating a new language solely as a sequence of texts to memorize. This was an educational proposal embodied in a printed object; it is not evidence that every teacher used it as intended.

The book also reveals the work needed to carry teaching across languages: editions, translation, images and printing joined the author’s programme. Its production belongs to a career shaped by religious refuge and patronage. Comparing the textbook with that career helps separate an aspiration for widespread education from the uneven resources and access through which actual pupils learned.
summary.zh:
《世界图解》将图像与词汇结合，使可见世界成为语言学习的一部分。拉丁语—德语原版1658年在纽伦堡出版，拉丁语—英语版于1659年在伦敦问世。这些日期表示所选版本，而非图像教学的起源，也不是该书使用的终点。

夸美纽斯的设计把学习与熟悉事物相连。明尼苏达大学展览介绍的内容包括地理、天气、植物、动物、机械以及宗教事务。图解页面提供了通过事物和活动讨论词语的方法，不必把新语言仅当成需要背诵的一连串文章。这是以印刷品表达的教育建议，并不能证明每位教师都按其意图使用。

书籍也显示教学跨越语言所需的工作：版本、翻译、图像与印刷共同参与作者的方案。它的制作属于一段受到宗教避难与资助关系塑造的生涯。把教材与人生相互比较，有助于区分普及教育的愿望，以及学生实际学习所依赖的不均等资源与机会。

dateNote.en: 1658–1659 follows the original Latin–German and first Latin–English editions. It does not date the beginning of all illustrated books or claim immediate universal classroom adoption.
dateNote.zh: 1658—1659年对应拉丁语—德语原版及首个拉丁语—英语版本，不是所有图解书的起点，也不表示课堂立即普遍采用。
